bug_semantics: A backend user with backend.manage_branding can persist attacker-controlled custom_css. BrandSetting::compileCss() concatenates that value into LESS input, and LESS escape syntax can preserve a literal </style><script> payload in the compiled output. The shared backend layout emits BrandSetting::renderCss() inside a style element, so an unsanitized cache miss or cache hit permits stored XSS for later backend-page viewers.
flaw_origin: Commit 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 is the smallest first-writer: it directly changed modules/backend/models/BrandSettings.php from parsing only bundled custom.less to parsing that file concatenated with self::get('custom_css'). Its immediate parent already had the settings/compiler framework but did not connect custom_css to the LESS parser. The commit is a one-parent direct source edit, not an aggregate, import, move, revert, or release carrier.
ai_marker: absent: git cat-file -p 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 shows one parent, human author and committer Sam Georges <sam@daftspunk.com>, and only the message 'Cache BrandSettings compiled CSS'; there is no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, bot identity, AI trailer, or other qualifying BIC-object signal.
evidence: The assigned first-party advisory data for GHSA-v7cf-8gh9-gxmj / CVE-2026-32257 describes the Brand Settings stored-XSS mechanism, declares winter/wn-backend-module <=1.2.12 affected and 1.2.13 first patched, and cites d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720. That establishes the advisory-linked fix_sha candidate but does not override contradictory source-path evidence.

git cat-file -p 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 resolves its sole parent as fbaab26bfbcfef96bac4802fd6dd62ec5557c8e7 and shows only human author/committer metadata with no AI marker. git diff fbaab26bfbcfef96bac4802fd6dd62ec5557c8e7 1203043a457dee3c298d7dd54289a866234cbb74 -- modules/backend/models/BrandSettings.php shows the direct causal edit: parse(File::get(...custom.less)) became parse(File::get(...custom.less).self::get('custom_css')). The parent file has no custom_css parser operand, proving immediate-parent absence and ruling out an aggregate, import, or move as the BIC.

The primary claimed d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720 was also the complete direct fix; the reviewer claimed it fixed only the cache-miss return and that c95d780ab54f3a3f74a94ae1667bf12b3c549d5d closed the remaining cache-hit path. Re-running git show d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720 -- modules/backend/models/BrandSetting.php proves the reviewer correct: d28f0 changes only the final return to strip_tags($customCss), while renderCss() still stores raw compiled attacker text with Cache::forever($cacheKey, $customCss) and returns Cache::get($cacheKey) unchanged on every cache hit.

git cat-file -p d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720 shows sole parent 29f823bb21742e10b758c5d1dfdf7a1297688edf, so d28f0 is a direct one-parent attempted source patch rather than an aggregate/import/move; it remains fix_sha because it is the advisory-cited patch, but it did not close the full vulnerable lifecycle.

git log --ancestry-path d28f0b9474af79cfaa80eeb9d691f7a7c4469720..c95d780ab54f3a3f74a94ae1667bf12b3c549d5d -- modules/backend/models/BrandSetting.php shows only intervening 130f0ea43e9228bf0d129b481da1cdfbcc4b4456 and c95d780ab54f3a3f74a94ae1667bf12b3c549d5d. git show 130f0ea43e9228bf0d129b481da1cdfbcc4b4456 changes LESS import resolution only and leaves the raw cache-hit return untouched, so it is not this XSS fix.

git show c95d780ab54f3a3f74a94ae1667bf12b3c549d5d -- modules/backend/models/BrandSetting.php modules/backend/tests/models/BrandSettingTest.php changes the cache-hit branch to return strip_tags(Cache::get($cacheKey)) and adds regressions for a second render and a pre-existing poisoned cache entry using the same style/script breakout. git cat-file -p c95d780ab54f3a3f74a94ae1667bf12b3c549d5d shows sole parent a56ef40be9e6c8a050b96895abce9fe9c22a1782, making c95d780 the direct, non-aggregate closing fix.

Version-boundary checks peel v1.2.12 to b6ac66c5e80ddc9ecd9211c10204cdcee6e14313, v1.2.13 to e09c8d3526f3583cb6c3476a021b885088ecd4bd, and v1.2.14 to 5f922c733a185f61b33eda674320c8690bffa4e2. git merge-base --is-ancestor succeeds for the BIC in v1.2.12, fails for d28f0 in v1.2.12, succeeds for d28f0 in v1.2.13, fails for c95d780 in v1.2.13, and succeeds for c95d780 in v1.2.14. git diff v1.2.13..v1.2.14 over BrandSetting.php reproduces the raw-cache-hit-to-strip_tags change. Therefore the advisory's published 1.2.13 boundary is incomplete in repository code; v1.2.14 is the first tag containing the full path closure.
reasoning: The BIC and its clean direct parent are undisputed and reverified: 1203043a first connects saved custom_css to LESS compilation, and its one-parent commit object contains no AI signal, so the gate-complete attribution verdict is NOT_AI. The fix disagreement is resolved by following both runtime branches rather than accepting the advisory reference alone. d28f0 sanitizes the cache-miss response but caches the unsanitized compiler result and returns that raw value on the next request. c95d780 directly sanitizes that cache-hit return and is the first commit whose containing release closes both cache states. Thus the reviewer wins the substantive disagreement: retain advisory-linked d28f0 as fix_sha, but use c95d780 as direct_fix_sha; the primary's claim that d28f0 fully fixed the vulnerability and that v1.2.13 was actually patched is disproved by the committed function and tag ancestry.
